subject: 9mmhandgun
label: 9mmhandgun, in the place of the game's models/v_9mmhandgun.mdl, models/p_9mmhandgun.mdl, models/w_9mmhandgun.mdl

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_satchel.mdl, models/w_grenade.mdl, models/w_357.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: Against the brief's 9mm pistol, the w_ outline in sides.png reads as a slab with a short cylinder at one end (LEFT, BACK, RIGHT). The angled grip is only hinted at by an offset block (TOP, BELOW), and no trigger guard or pistol profile shows. The first-person view (first-person.png, left) reads more like a pistol than the w_ model does.

M2.reason: The brief gives no size, so there is nothing to hold the measured [20.9, 5.9, 21.4] against within 15%. The proportions are doubtful for a sidearm: in FRONT and LEFT the body is about three times as long as it is tall, while the measured height is about equal to the length.

M3.reason: Parts a 9mm pistol needs: slide, barrel, frame and grip, trigger guard, trigger, magazine, front and rear sights. The asset has a block body, a grey cap block, a black offset block that may be the grip, and a stub at one end. The trigger guard, a clear magazine and the sights are missing, so M3 is capped at 1. The p_ model (in-hand.png) shows no trigger guard either.

M4.reason: Black and grey, as the brief asks: dark near-black blocks (grip/slide body in FRONT-LEFT and BACK-LEFT) with lighter grey panels and a grey stub. Reads as polymer and steel. No measured colour difference supplied, so judged by eye.

M5.reason: The brief asks for no markings. The asset has one dark side slot in RIGHT and FRONT-RIGHT and a light bevel band. It has no slide serrations, grip texture or ejection port, which a 9mm pistol would normally show. M5 is not a must-have item.

M6.reason: In lineup.png the asset (A) is a dark block with grey caps, and a player would not take it for a 9mm pistol. The first-person view (first-person.png, left) is closer to a pistol, so it is not a plain box, but the w_ model is clearly off next to the .357 (C) and the grenade (D).

M7.reason: The brief names no front, and the w_ model lies on its side in FRONT and LEFT. Nothing in the views shows which end is the front or that it stands on its origin as a pistol lies, so this cannot be confirmed. The first-person model points up and forward as the game's does.

M8.reason: SMAK's check passed with no errors. The asset has 116 triangles, under twice Half-Life's median of its kind (142, so 284 is the limit). Nothing visible is open, inside out or clearly floating, though the separate blocks in TOP and BELOW are not fully checkable from pictures.

W1.reason: At rest in first-person.png the asset sits where the game's pistol does, roughly on the same screen spot and the same way round, with its grip in the orange hand. In attack.png frame 2/14 the gun swings up and out while the hand stays low, so the grip looks like it lifts clear of the hand. Frames 4 to 14 hold it in place.
